column1: # EVERY CLASS A BOUNDARY-DECLARING OBLIGATION COULD LAND ON: every concrete
# and `tests/`, with the two facts that decide which interface should carry the
# obligation — whether the class is a hierarchical parent, and whether it is
# WHY THIS FILE EXISTS SEPARATELY FROM THE POPULATION TABLE. The population
# table enumerates the (channel, level) PATHS the consumer walks; this one
# enumerates CLASSES. The difference is not empty, and the plan's first draft
# reasoned about classes from the path table and missed six of them: the five
# the walk never resolves to because it calls `forLevel()` first, and
# `ComputedMetricRuleOptions`, whose rule declares no channel statically.
# COUNTS: 55 concrete implementors — 45 in `src/`, 10 test doubles.
# 28 of them are `ThresholdAwareOptionsInterface`: the 27 production classes
# test double (`SubjectControlOptions`). No hierarchical parent is among them,
# WHAT THIS DECIDES. Cross-checked against the population table: every row that
# resolves to a number is `threshold_aware=yes`, and no `threshold_aware=no` row
# holds a warning-named member. Putting the obligation on
# `ThresholdAwareOptionsInterface` therefore reaches every holder of a boundary
# while leaving 27 classes untouched — including all five parents, for which no
# honest answer exists, and the ~17 occurrence detectors, which would otherwise
# gain a constant-returning method that touches no field.
# WHAT THIS METHOD DOES NOT SEE
# - Classes are found by loading every `*.php` under `src/` and `tests/` and
#   asking reflection. A class declared in a file whose namespace or class name
#   the loader's two regexes miss (multiple classes per file are read; classes
#   built by `eval` or by a string-keyed factory are not) is absent.
# - Anonymous classes implementing either interface inside a test method are not
#   reachable by reflection over declared classes, so they are absent from the
#   rows below. They were counted separately by grep
#   (`grep -rn 'new class' tests --include='*.php' -A3`): SIX of them, in
#   `ThresholdAwareOptionsInterface` leaves all six untouched and an obligation
# - Classes outside this repository. The project has no external rule authors by
#   policy, so this is a stated non-coverage rather than a measured zero.
